name: TN-01
label: Safe R

key_factors: District's R+29 partisan lean makes it one of the most Republican-held seats in the country
Harshbarger holds an enormous financial edge: roughly $2.0 million on hand versus about $14,000 for Burke
Incumbent Harshbarger is renominated and faces no outside spending against her
Prediction markets price the Republican at about 99 percent
model.rationale: The seat's R+29 lean, Harshbarger's cash advantage of roughly $2 million to $14,000, and markets pricing her at 99 percent all point the same direction, with no polls or headlines suggesting any competition. Nothing in the evidence justifies moving from a safe Republican read in the low-20s.
model.watch: Only a major late-breaking scandal or a historically large polling and turnout error across East Tennessee would put this seat in play.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Diana Harshbarger enters the general election as a heavy favorite in a northeast Tennessee district that voted about 29 points more Republican than the nation in recent cycles. She is a renominated incumbent with roughly $2 million in cash on hand, and no outside groups are spending against her.

Challenger Kristi Burke has raised about $102,000 total with only about $14,000 left, and several independent candidates are also on the ballot but without visible campaigns. No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, but prediction markets give Burke about a 2 percent chance. The expected margin sits in the low 20s for Harshbarger, with uncertainty mainly reflecting the absence of polling rather than any sign of competitiveness.
